issues.quote: Madame and I sat down to piquet in the salon. Odile plays a hard game, Inspector, and a cold one.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says "Madame" began to play the piano. The transcript never states that Odile is Madame; it only introduces the name Odile after Madame has been used, and later says "Odile began to play the piano."
issues.misreading: A solver could take Odile to be a different woman in the house, which would make the piano-playing witness someone other than Madame and break the alibi chain. The sheet's identification is only implied.

issues.quote: Aurèle asked us all to show him our watches. He does it every year. It is his joke and his tyranny. Mine was two minutes ahead of the bell.
issues.fact: D1 says the watch inspection happened at the moment the temple bell struck nine. The transcript answers the question about the bell but does not say the inspection happened at that moment, only that it happened at dinner.
issues.misreading: A solver could read the inspection as occurring at some other point during dinner, not at the striking of nine, so the two-minute offset would not be tied to the nine o'clock bell.

issues.quote: The old Morbier. It strikes by its own face, and one learns to listen to it as one listens to a difficult patient.
issues.fact: The fact sheet says only that the hall clock struck eleven a moment after Dr Vauthier sat down again. It gives no information about how the clock works or whether it is reliable.
issues.misreading: The remark that the clock 'strikes by its own face' and must be listened to could suggest the clock is idiosyncratic or unreliable, inviting a solver to doubt its reading against the watch.
